Select Parameters for a Comparison Plot

Source: R/f_comparison_plot.R
getComparisonPlotParameters.Rd

Proposes axes and an object category without creating a plot. Selection problems are returned as text so applications can display them before plotting.

Usage

getComparisonPlotParameters(
  data,
  xParamName = NULL,
  yParamName = NULL,
  ...,
  categoryParamName = NULL,
  groupParamName = NULL,
  objects = NULL,
  yAxisSide = "auto"
)

Arguments

data

A comparison data frame, a TrialComparison, or its summary.

xParamName, yParamName

Optional explicit axis column names. yParamName may be a vector of distinct numeric columns. Automatic axes must be varying numeric columns. Every y column must be numeric; an explicitly selected x-axis may also be categorical.

...

Further arguments. Currently unused.

categoryParamName

Optional character vector of category column names. All selected columns jointly define the categories. NULL selects objectName, objectNumber, or designNumber, in that order, when it identifies multiple objects and is not selected as an axis or group. NA_character_ disables automatic categories, as does character(0). No category is needed for a single object.

groupParamName

Optional explicit grouping column.

objects

Optional original objects for role-aware selection when data is a data frame. A TrialComparison supplies its own objects automatically.

yAxisSide

Axis assignment: "auto" (default), "left", or "right". Supply one value for all y parameters, a vector in their order, or a named vector assigning individual parameters. Unspecified named entries remain automatic. The same argument is accepted by plotComparison().

Value

A list containing xParamName, yParamName, categoryParamName, groupParamName, yAxisSide, yAxisTransformation, yAxisRanges, message, candidates, and issues. yAxisSide is named by the selected parameters; the right-axis plotting transformation is value * scale + offset from yAxisTransformation. yAxisRanges contains the reference ranges used for scaling, not ggplot's expanded panel limits. Unresolved selections are NULL. message is NULL on success, otherwise contains all selection problems. candidates lists eligible columns for each selection; issues contains diagnostic metadata used by plotComparison().

Details

Explicit selections prevail. When original objects are available, inputs and design settings are preferred for x and results for y, as in the comparison plot method. Without original objects, only varying numeric columns determine automatic axes. Identifiers are excluded, but stages remain eligible. An omitted axis is selected only when exactly one eligible candidate remains. Ambiguity, invalid column selections, and unsupported data structures are returned without raising a selection error. A category may remain NULL without an error when no object category is available or required. The data and the original objects are not changed, and no ggplot2 installation is required.

Automatic y-axis assignment uses the largest gap between finite nonzero parameter magnitudes (maximum absolute values). A gap of at least a factor of ten separates the smaller scale onto the right axis. Otherwise all parameters share the left axis. Consistent explicit reversals also reverse automatic assignments; explicit assignments always prevail. There are at most two shared scales, with no separate normalization within either side. Dual-axis reference ranges include zero. Probability-like ranges within numerical tolerance of [0, 1], with maximum at least 0.1, use [0, 1]. Smaller magnitudes retain their observed range. Constant zero or entirely missing ranges use [0, 1] to avoid a degenerate transformation.

Examples

comparison <- getComparison(
    first = getDesignFixed(alpha = 0.025),
    second = getDesignFixed(alpha = 0.05)
)
selection <- getComparisonPlotParameters(comparison, yParamName = "criticalValues")
selection[c("xParamName", "yParamName", "categoryParamName", "message")]
#> $xParamName
#> [1] "alpha"
#> 
#> $yParamName
#> [1] "criticalValues"
#> 
#> $categoryParamName
#> [1] "objectName"
#> 
#> $message
#> NULL
#>
